answer: Sybil resistance here is a proof-of-work gate that prices every extra identity in real electricity. A newcomer must find a nonce whose hash beats an epoch target, and that work is tied to the address, so one machine cannot mint a thousand identities for free: each pays its own fresh search. The anchor binds rewards to one address, so spreading effort across clones earns no discount, and clones crowding a narrow lagoon of hashes compete for the same slot, burning power without better payout odds. Miners on any knoll reject work that misses the target. The bill is N times per-identity compute.
